issues.title: Arbitrary-scale append-column Gram bound
issues.failure_explanation: The true Gram matrix is diag(B^TB, gamma^2||x+y||_2^2) plus a purely off-diagonal block. The later old decomposition instead uses diag(B^TB,1) and a perturbation whose lower-right entry is gamma^2||x+y||_2^2, so it is not an equality. Moreover, the extremal eigenvalues of diag(B^TB,1) are max{sigma_max^2(B),1} and min{sigma_min^2(B),1}, not necessarily the extrema of B^TB alone.
issues.overall_effect: The first append-column estimate in thm:cool is false, and the normalized consequence derived from that estimate is not established by the given proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false Gram decomposition by the actual one. Writing s = γ²‖x+y‖₂² and c = |γ|‖Bᵀy‖₂, Weyl's inequalities give, whenever min{σ_min²(B),s}>c, κ([B,γ(x+y)]) ≤ sqrt((max{σ_max²(B),s}+c)/(min{σ_min²(B),s}−c)). Then specialize to s=1 for the normalized column and rederive a corresponding normalized consequence, using the correct max/min extrema and an explicit positivity condition.
issues.why_classification: The old estimate has materially false scale behavior: even with y=0, letting γ tend to zero makes the true condition number diverge while the displayed bound can remain finite. Thus a same-strength local edit is unavailable. A comparable arbitrary-scale and normalized append-column theorem is nevertheless recovered by a contained Gram-matrix/Weyl argument, without global reconstruction or major loss.

issues.title: Incorrect zero-noncentrality branch of the Marcum-Q definition
issues.failure_explanation: From the n=0 term of the supplied Bessel series, alpha^{1-M} I_{M-1}(alpha x) tends to x^{M-1}/(2^{M-1}Gamma(M)). The defining integral therefore tends to (1/(2^{M-1}Gamma(M))) times the integral from beta to infinity of x^{2M-1} exp(-x^2/2) dx. Substitution u=x^2/2 gives Gamma(M,beta^2/2)/Gamma(M), contradicting the displayed beta^2 branch.
issues.overall_effect: All uses with positive noncentrality are unaffected, but the old norm and projection formulas at zero signal use the wrong centered chi-square scaling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Γ(M,β²)/Γ(M) by Γ(M,β²/2)/Γ(M) in the α=0 branch of the Marcum-Q definition, and read every dependent zero-signal formula with that corrected branch.
issues.why_classification: The preceding integral and supplied Bessel series uniquely force the argument β²/2 via the substitution u=x²/2. This is a single transcriptional scaling error; the positive-noncentrality branch, proof architecture, and substantive probability statements require no further repair.

issues.title: Incorrect noncentral-F law for the normalized residual

failure_location.quote: Since $Z_1 \sim \chi^2_n$, $Z_2 \sim \chi'^2_{m-n}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2^2}{\sigma^2}\right)$, therefore, by Chapter 6, equation 40 of \cite{patnaik1949non}, we have:

issues.failure_explanation: For epsilon_1>0, the old derivation correctly reaches an event Z_2/Z_1 >= epsilon_2/epsilon_1. Since the noncentral-F ratio is formed from Z_2^2 and Z_1^2, its threshold must be n epsilon_2^2/((m-n)epsilon_1^2), and the required probability is one minus the CDF at that threshold. The old statement instead uses an unsquared threshold and no upper-tail complement. It is also undefined at its advertised endpoint epsilon_1=0.
issues.overall_effect: The exact residual probability is wrong, so the probability asserted by cor-main and propagated into the old multi-step QR result is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use U=Z₂²/σ² and V=Z₁²/σ² as the chi-square variables. For ε₁>0, replace the stated probability by 1−F'_{m−n,n}(nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²);‖X‖₂²/σ²). Treat ε₁=0 separately, where the displayed event has probability zero, and propagate the squared threshold and upper-tail complement through the listed dependent probability formulas.
issues.why_classification: The old derivation already reaches the required ratio event; the defect is a routine local failure to square the norms and retain the upper-tail complement. Correcting those steps preserves the same model, event, exact noncentral-F law, and downstream proof structure, with no new lemma or substantive restriction. It is not a typo because the proof makes an invalid distributional inference.

issues.title: Missing input contract in the single-step QR corollary

failure_location.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \)

issues.failure_explanation: The prose and formula use q without introducing it, and full rank does not imply the unit-column hypothesis of cor:cond-ls. This is material: scaling an otherwise orthonormal B by a small scalar leaves kappa(B)=1 but can make kappa([B,q]) arbitrarily large, so the claimed kappa(B)-only transfer cannot hold for arbitrary full-rank B.
issues.overall_effect: The single-step corollary is not well-defined and its residual-to-condition invocation is outside the cited corollary's hypotheses. The old multi-step corollary consequently lacks a valid stated one-step dependency, even though its intended normalized columns satisfy the repaired contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that B has full column rank and unit-norm columns, let B=QR, and define q=(X+Y)/‖X+Y‖₂ on the almost-sure event X+Y≠0, with X in range(P_Q^⊥). Apply the unit-column residual-to-condition result under this contract and carry the same contract into the multi-step invocation, whose previously computed normalized columns already satisfy it.
issues.why_classification: Defining q is local, but the unit-column premise cannot be omitted: arbitrary rescaling leaves κ(B) unchanged while making κ([B,q]) arbitrarily large. Restricting the coherent all-full-rank statement to the source-supported normalized QR regime is therefore a meaningful input-class weakening, so the issue exceeds minor. The repair remains contained and leaves a recognizably comparable single- and multi-step chain.

issues.title: Incorrect residual-to-condition multiplier
issues.failure_explanation: The cited unit-column residual bound gives the multiplier f(r)=(1+sqrt(1-r^2))/r. On the residual event r>=t, monotonicity yields f(r)<=f(t)=sqrt(1+(epsilon_1/epsilon_2)^2)+epsilon_1/epsilon_2. Thus the proof, after granting its valid inputs, supports a different multiplier from the one in the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative single-step condition-number guarantee is false, and the same incorrect factors invalidate the condition-number product in the old multi-step corollary independently of its probability defects.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let a=ε₁/ε₂ and t=(1+a²)^(−1/2). Replace the asserted multiplier by (1+sqrt(1−t²))/t = sqrt(1+a²)+a. Make the same replacement, with indexed parameters, in every factor of the multi-step product; equivalently, parameterize directly by t or τ.
issues.why_classification: The correction is locally derivable, but it materially weakens the advertised quantitative guarantee: under a common rescaling of ε₁ and ε₂ the event is unchanged while the old multiplier can be made arbitrarily smaller than the valid one. Because the corrected single-step and product bounds remain recognizably comparable and need no new proof architecture, the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Incorrect per-step dimensions and parameter interface in the QR product corollary
issues.failure_explanation: Instantiating cor-main with B equal to the first i-1 computed columns requires replacing its column count n by i-1. The old proof instead uses degrees of freedom (m-i,i), and its displayed bound contains w_i, which is nowhere defined. Consequently the claimed probability is not the result of any well-typed one-step invocation, even if conditioning and the one-step formulas are otherwise repaired.
issues.overall_effect: The final corollary's probability expression remains undefined and dimensionally off by one independently of its adaptive-aggregation, tail, and multiplier defects.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At step i instantiate the one-step result with i−1 existing columns. Thus use degrees of freedom (m−i+1,i−1), use the defined ideal residual a_i rather than the undefined w_i for the noncentrality parameter, and consistently index ε_{1,i} and ε_{2,i} in both statement and proof.
issues.why_classification: This is a local, routine correction of the one-step parameter substitution and notation. It preserves the algorithm, probability-law structure, scope, and resulting product guarantee without a new argument or meaningful loss. It is more than a typo because the displayed parameters make the cited theorem invocation mathematically ill-typed.

issues.title: Invalid unconditional aggregation in the adaptive QR process
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof substitutes the history-dependent noncentrality parameter ||a_i||_2^2/sigma^2 directly into an unconditional probability statement. Conditional application would instead give a random conditional failure probability whose expectation enters the unconditional union bound. No conditioning, measurability contract, expectation, or deterministic bound on that parameter is supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The stated multi-step success probability is not a well-defined unconditional numerical guarantee, independently of the separate one-step formula and indexing defects.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce the filtration generated by the past perturbations, require a_i to be measurable with respect to the past and e_i to be conditionally independent N(0,σ²I), and write p_i(a_i)=P(E_i^c | F_{i−1}) using the valid one-step law. Replace the random plug-in lower bound by the unconditional bound P(∩_i E_i) ≥ 1−Σ_i E[p_i(a_i)], obtained from the tower property and union bound, while retaining the same product implication on ∩_i E_i.
issues.why_classification: A genuine adaptive-conditioning argument and an explicit measurability/independence contract are required. Moreover, the central random plug-in probability must be replaced by an averaged unconditional guarantee rather than merely edited symbolically, so the issue exceeds minor. The filtration and tower-property repair is contained, and the multi-step product conclusion survives in a recognizably comparable form, precluding a serious classification.
